title: [0.100] Command Palette: incorrect dock position on 2nd display
author: watchmakerful

judgment.rationale: The original Windhawk-sensitive report is now supplemented by a detailed 0.100.2 reproduction on a second monitor with equal resolution and scaling and no Windhawk. That materially establishes a native multi-monitor dock positioning defect.
evidence: The original report shows a huge, incorrectly positioned dock on the secondary display.
Disabling the Taskbar on Top mod avoided the original configuration.
A later reporter reproduced a closely related second-monitor failure on 0.100.2 without Windhawk.
The later setup uses equal 1920x1080 displays at 100% scaling and the failure follows monitor 2 rather than Windows primary-display selection.
judgment.recommended_action: Queue a focused Command Palette dock monitor-geometry investigation; retain Windhawk as one amplifier, not the sole cause.

fix_assessment.rationale: The multi-monitor defect is reproducible, but lightweight evidence does not establish the faulty coordinate/scaling calculation.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette Dock can become oversized or misplaced on a secondary monitor, including on systems without Windhawk.
known_information: Changing the Windows primary display did not move the failure away from monitor 2 for the later reporter.
Windhawk Taskbar on Top can trigger or amplify one variant.
inferences: Per-monitor work-area or display-identity handling is a plausible area, but not a proven root cause.
issue_context.analysis: The newer independent reproduction removes the prior dependency on a third-party taskbar modification and makes code-level triage appropriate.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the current public issue body, labels, assignees, and up to the latest 20 public comments returned by GitHub.
Kept the existing dashboard read-only; no dashboard files were modified or published.

actions.label: Queue CmdPal dock multi-monitor investigation
actions.note: Draft candidate only; no comment or other write was made to microsoft/PowerToys.

comment.body: The later 0.100.2 report establishes that a closely related secondary-monitor Dock positioning failure also occurs without Windhawk, on equal-resolution 100%-scale displays, and remains on monitor 2 after primary-display changes. This is enough to investigate Command Palette Dock's per-monitor work-area and placement handling; Windhawk should be retained as an additional trigger rather than treated as the sole cause.
